text:
leo: noticed two nodes in us-west-2 reporting intermittent ECC Xid bursts on p4 cards, pods getting evicted. putting a quick triage thread here.
maria: ugh, saw alerts. any recent firmware pushes or kernel bumps to that fleet? :thinking_face:
leo: no infra deploys in the last 24h. I pulled the dmesg from one of the nodes, snippet below.
leo: ```[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=4321, GPU=0
[ 1234.567941] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] kernel: nvidia: probe of 0000:65:00 failed with error -110
``` 
ana: thanks. can you run `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERR` and `journalctl -k --no-pager -n 200` and paste? small outputs ok.
leo: pasted outputs to a gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/triage-2148123456 (shortened). main bit: memory errors + ECC corrected counts rising on GPU0.
sam: is this single-card failing or multiple GPUs on node? could be PCIe riser or power on the host.
maria: also check `lspci -vvv` for link state and `ethtool -i`? sometimes PCIe resets correlate with firmware.
leo: quick `nvidia-smi` snapshot:
leo: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54.03    Driver Version: 535.54.03    
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-80G  On         | 00000065:00:00.0 Off |                    12 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
``` 
ana: 12 volatile uncorr ECC is concerning. if it's >0 and growing during workload that's a hard fail.
ops-bot: @infra-sre noted incident created: INC-2148
sam: immediate playbook I'd do:
- stop workloads on the node (cordon + drain, --ignore-daemonsets)
- capture full logs (`/var/log/messages`, `journalctl -u docker -b`, `dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.txt`)
- run hardware-level checks: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` & PSU logs from iDrac/AMT
- try a soft reset: `echo 1 > /proc/driver/nvidia/reset` (only if safe for your environment)
maria: also snapshot nv-host engine and kvcache traces if you can. we want to rule out memory corruption vs driver bug.
leo: performing drain now: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-usw2-13 && kubectl drain node/gpu-usw2-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` : will upload artifacts to longterm bucket.
ana: if drain fails due to stuck pods, `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` for the offenders. note data loss risk.
sam: if problem reproduces after reboot, schedule replacement. flaky cards waste cycles; don't waste time re-queuing.
leo: reboots queued; created snapshot tar: `/tmp/gpu-triage-2148123456.tar.gz` includes dmesg, journal, nvidia-smi logs, lspci output.
maria: please also add `/var/crash` and `nv-host-logs` if present. tag the bucket object with node and time.
ops-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-gpu-triage/2148123456/gpu-usw2-13.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
leo: after reboot the GPU came back but ECC corrected keeps climbing under stress test. isolating node from prod.
ana: create a quick flame-test: run memtest on the card or run a CUDA memstress for 30m to see if ECC increases linearly.
sam: capture power draw from IPMI while running stress; if power spikes correlate, could be PSU or connector.
maria: for long term: adding a health-exporter that emits ECC counts per-minute to metrics would help catch earlier. also consider a lightweight NVSMI sidecar to snapshot on Xid events.
leo: agree. opening a short RFC for a minimal exporter: push ECC/corrected/uncorrected + Xid events to prometheus pushgateway when >0.
ops-bot: created task: TASK-2148 (add-ecc-metrics-exporter)
maria: for now, replacement scheduled for tomorrow; marking node as decommission candidate if replacement card shows same behaviour.
leo: thanks all, closing loop here. will post postmortem if replacement doesn't fix it. :thumbsup:
